## Findings to know
- taskkill form chosen: `taskkill //T //F //PID <winpid>` (winpid from /proc/<pid>/winpid). All three forms (`//T //F //PID`, `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 taskkill /T /F /PID`, `cmd //c "taskkill ..."`) killed a throwaway sleep (rc 0, gone). None follows a child whose forked parent already died (a `bash -c 'sleep & sleep & wait'` left both sleeps), so kill_tree walks ps -ef first and takes every member down by its own winpid, kept alongside the plain kill.
- Stale waiter cause: wait-run.sh run_ended judges the log by its last ` start at ` line. A waiter that starts before the restarted runner has written that line sees the previous run's STOPPED (a PAUSED stop) and returns exit 1 at once. The old ignore rule only helps after the new start line exists. Fix: `--since <epoch taken before the restart>`; until a start line at or after it exists the call answers 4, after 5 minutes 5 (NO START). Reproduced in run-stops 6b (old behaviour exit 1).
- My own `python -` call waited on stdin for 5 minutes during this batch: lesson P-tune4-1 (flash-lessons Proposed, 3 candidates added).
- brief-check pins WARN does not use probe-deps: probe-deps is about stubs for new types; the pins rule reuses brief-check's own search_item.
- over-cap apply relies on flash.sh applying a nonzero-worker job's files (it does for every result but 3, 4 and apply failures); result 1 is assumed to be the CLI's turn-cap exit.
- Not verified on a live batch: hung guard (tested with stubs), idle poll cost of `find` on a real job worktree.
- Pre-existing uncommitted change tools/tests/agent-cost-test.sh (+10 lines, not mine) left unstaged.
